State Cache Behavior

State Cache Behavior provides an authoritative extension point that enables TTL-based entity caching within a FeatureCell. This behavior coordinates cache lookup, cache-miss resolution, and cache refresh through the FeatureCell state pipeline.

State cache behavior integrates directly with state resolution and finalization. Cached entities are populated exclusively from finalized state emissions and refreshed through controlled pipeline execution.

This behavior does not replace state ownership or pipeline semantics. It augments a FeatureCell with a deterministic cache surface while preserving a single, authoritative source of truth.

State Cache Extension

When enabled, the State Cache Behavior extends the FeatureCell API with cache lookup methods that resolve entities by identifier. Cache lookups are coordinated through the FeatureCell pipeline and respect lifecycle boundaries, error handling, and state finalization.

Cached entities are stored with a defined time-to-live (TTL). When a cache entry expires or does not exist, resolution is triggered through the pipeline using a configured fetch strategy. All cached values originate exclusively from finalized state emissions.

Cache behavior operates as an authoritative extension. It does not mutate state directly and does not bypass pipeline execution. Instead, it reacts to committed state snapshots and augments the FeatureCell with deterministic lookup semantics.

Fluent Configuration

State cache behavior is registered using the FeatureCell fluent API. Configuration is declared explicitly during FeatureCell initialization using withStateCache() and is consumed during FeatureCell activation.

Notes
  • Cache lookup APIs and state update APIs coexist. The FeatureCell continues to expose replaceState() and mergeState() alongside cacheLookup() and cacheLookup$(). Direct state updates remain valid. When cache behavior is enabled, cache lookup APIs provide TTL evaluation and pending-lookup coordination for identifier-based resolution.
  • Direct state updates update cached values without resetting TTL. When state is updated through replaceState() or mergeState(), any resolved entities that correspond to existing cache entries update the cached value but preserve the original expiration window. TTL is established only when an entity is first recorded in the cache.
  • Expired entries may refresh without a lookup. When an entry expires, refresh can be initiated by the cache refresh loop, in addition to lookup-driven refresh. All refresh execution still occurs through the FeatureCell pipeline.
  • Interceptors can influence cache refresh timing. Cache-miss and TTL-expiration refreshes are resolved through the FeatureCell pipeline. Interceptors such as debounce, delay, throttling, or conditional gating may delay or suppress resolution execution. When such interceptors are present, cache refresh execution timing is affected by the interceptor policy.
  • Lifecycle alignment is preserved. Cache state is reset or destroyed in coordination with the owning FeatureCell lifecycle, ensuring that cached data never outlives the FeatureCell that produced it.
  • Filters may intentionally discard resolved entities. FeatureCell filters may remove or suppress a resolved entity during pipeline evaluation, resulting in a finalized undefined value even when the entity exists in upstream state or is available from a remote source. In this case, the corresponding cache entry is removed and pending lookups resolve as undefined.
Design Decisions

State cache behavior is designed to integrate deterministically with the FeatureCell pipeline while preserving explicit lifecycle control, immutability guarantees, and predictable resolution semantics. The following table documents how the cache responds to key runtime conditions and lifecycle events.

State Cache Design Decisions
Condition Behavior
No Cache Hit When no cached entry exists for the requested identifier, a cache-miss resolution is triggered through the FeatureCell pipeline using the configured fetch strategy. The lookup resolves only after state finalization and cache recording complete.
Cache Hit (TTL Valid) When a resolved entity exists in cached state for the requested identifier and its TTL has not expired, the cached entity is returned immediately without triggering pipeline execution or state resolution.
Undefined Resolution When a finalized state emission resolves to undefined for a specific identifier, the corresponding cache entry is removed. Any pending lookups for that identifier are resolved as undefined. Other cached entries remain unaffected.
Null Resolution (State Clear) A finalized state emission with a null value is treated as an authoritative state clear. All cached entries are removed, all pending lookups are resolved as undefined, and cache state is fully reset.
TTL Expired When a cached entry expires, refresh may be initiated by lookup or by the refresh loop through the FeatureCell pipeline. Until finalization completes, concurrent lookups are fan-out coordinated and resolved together.
Concurrent Lookups Multiple concurrent lookups for the same identifier are coordinated through a shared pending resolution. Only one pipeline resolution is initiated; all awaiting callers are resolved together when finalization completes.
replaceState / mergeState Updates State updates applied through replaceState() or mergeState() update cached entity values when identifiers match. These updates do not reset or extend the existing TTL associated with the cache entry.
FeatureCell Reset A FeatureCell reset clears all cached entries, resolves all pending lookups as undefined, and halts any in-progress refresh operations. Cache state does not survive a reset.
FeatureCell Destroy When the owning FeatureCell is destroyed, all cache state is cleared, all pending lookups are resolved as undefined, and all cache-related subscriptions and refresh loops are terminated.
Pipeline Error (Scoped) When an error is finalized for a specific identifier, the corresponding cache entry is removed and any pending lookups for that identifier resolve as undefined.
Pipeline Error (Global) When an error is finalized without an identifier scope, all pending lookups resolve as undefined. Cached entries remain subject to subsequent state emissions and lifecycle events.
State Cache Diagram
Cache Lookup API

When state cache behavior is enabled, the FeatureCell runtime surface is extended with dedicated cache lookup methods.

  • cacheLookup(id) — resolves a cached entity by identifier and returns a Promise that completes when the entity is available.
  • cacheLookup$(id) — resolves a cached entity by identifier and returns an Observable that emits once and completes.

Both lookup methods coordinate cache hits, cache misses, and refresh behavior through the state pipeline. Pending lookups for the same identifier are fan-out coordinated and resolved together.

If pipeline finalization does not produce an entity for the requested identifier (for example: filtered output, scoped error finalization, or cache entry removal), lookup resolution completes with undefined.

Configuration

Enables TTL-based entity caching for a FeatureCell. Cached entities are indexed by a configured identifier key and populated from authoritative state emissions.

Cache misses and refresh operations trigger state merges using the configured fetch strategy.

FeatureCell Initialization

The State Cache Behavior exposes a fluent configuration API that allows engineers to register cache options during FeatureCell initialization.

This API does not perform caching directly. It records configuration that is later consumed by the State Cache Behavior during FeatureCell activation.

Fluent State Cache Configuration
Fluent API Description

withStateCache(options)

input:

  • options: StateCacheBehaviorOptions<T>

returns: FeatureCellBaseShape (chainable)

Registers state cache configuration for a FeatureCell. The supplied options define cache lifetime, entity identification, and cache-miss resolution strategy.

This method must be called before initialize(). When invoked, it stores cache configuration that is consumed by the State Cache Behavior during activation.

Multiple calls overwrite prior cache configuration.
Usage
Cache Lookup APIs
API Description

cacheLookup(id: string)

inputs:

  • id: string

returns:

  • Promise<TEntity>

Performs a cache lookup for the specified entity identifier. If a valid cached entry exists, the cached entity is returned immediately.

If the entry is missing or expired, the lookup triggers a cache-miss resolution through the FeatureCell state pipeline using the configured fetch strategy. The returned promise resolves when lookup finalization completes. If finalization does not produce an entity, the promise resolves with undefined.

Concurrent lookups for the same identifier are automatically fan-out coordinated and resolved together.

cacheLookup$(id: string)

inputs:

  • id: string

returns:

  • Observable<TEntity>

Reactive variant of cacheLookup. Emits the resolved entity (or undefined when finalization produces no entity) and then completes.

This API integrates cache lookup into reactive workflows while preserving the same cache-miss resolution, fan-out coordination, and pipeline semantics as the promise-based variant.

The observable emits exactly once per invocation and completes.

State Cache Examples

Example 1: Configure State Cache Behavior

{{`@FeatureCell`}}<Employee[][]>{{`('employees')
@Injectable({
  providedIn: 'root'
})
export class EmployeeService {
  private readonly vault = injectVault`}}<Employee[][]>{{`(EmployeeService);

  constructor() {
    // Assumes withStateCacheBehavior is registered during FeatureCell setup (provideFeatureCell)
    this.vault
      .withStateCache({
        ttl: CacheTTL.FiveMinutes,
        idKey: 'id',
        fetchType: ResolveType.Promise,
        fetch: (id) => fetchEmployeeById(id)
      })
      .initialize();
  }
}`}}
 
{{`export const employeeCell = FeatureCell`}}<Employee[]>{{`(
  {
    key: 'employees',
    initialState: [],
  },
  [
    withStateCacheBehavior
  ]
);

// Executed during application startup (e.g. app.config.ts)
employeeCell
  .withStateCache({
    ttl: CacheTTL.FiveMinutes,
    idKey: 'id',
    fetchType: ResolveType.Promise,
    fetch: (id) => fetchEmployeeById(id)
  })
  .initialize();`}}

Example 2: Lookup a Cached Entity

{{`// Promise-based lookup
const employee = await this.vault.cacheLookup('123');

// Observable-based lookup
this.vault.cacheLookup$('123').subscribe(emp => {
  console.info(emp);
});`}}
 
{{`// Promise-based lookup
const employee = await employeeCell.cacheLookup('123');

// Observable-based lookup
employeeCell.cacheLookup$('123').subscribe(emp => {
  console.info(emp);
});`}}
